answer: A reputation bond works like a velvet rope with teeth: every agent must lock a stake that vests slowly, so a hollow identity with no history cannot buy trust instantly. Newcomers start at the bottom of a bridge of small, verified tasks, and only consistent, useful work raises their limit. An attacker spinning up thousands of clones must fund each stake and wait out the same slow climb, so the cost scales with every fake identity while honest agents pay almost nothing.
